title: House Budget Committee schedules mark-up as tax and regulatory updates advance in July
text:
House Budget Committee schedules mark-up as tax and regulatory updates advance in July
The House Budget Committee is set to meet on Thursday, July 15, to mark up a budget resolution as President Trump urges Congress to prioritize passing a new reconciliation bill following the enactment of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R. 6644), which became law after he neither signed nor vetoed it at midnight Friday.
Congress returns this week with the Senate scheduled for four weeks in session before the August recess and the House for two weeks. The House had left early during its last sessions in June due to difficulties within the Republican majority over procedural rules. President Trump called on July 7 for Congress to make passing a budget reconciliation bill their “Number One Priority,” including $350 billion for defense and provisions from THE SAVE AMERICA ACT.
The proposed budget resolution would allow up to $95 billion in additional spending, with committee instructions aligning with recent White House requests for supplemental funding in defense and agriculture, as well as up to $10 billion related to election rules under the SAVE America Act. However, no instructions were given to the Committee on Ways and Means, meaning tax provisions are not eligible for inclusion in this reconciliation bill. The resolution lacks Senate instructions; unless these are added before it reaches the floor, another vote will be needed after Senate passage. Even if enacted in July, Congress is not expected to address the reconciliation bill until just before Labor Day unless an unusual August return occurs.
Senate Majority Leader John Thune said that further supplemental appropriations could be included within broader appropriations legislation or a continuing resolution expected by September, when government funding is set to lapse at fiscal year-end. Meanwhile, Senator Lindsey Graham of South Carolina passed away suddenly Saturday evening; Governor Henry McMaster appointed Graham’s sister Darline Graham Nordone as his replacement, who was sworn into office Tuesday. Senator Ron Johnson of Wisconsin is anticipated as next chairman of the Senate Budget Committee.
In judicial developments, the Court of Federal Claims invalidated Treasury Regulation § 1.951A-2(c)(5) concerning GILTI disqualified basis rules following Keysight Technologies v. United States (July 2). The court found Treasury lacked statutory authority under section 7805(a) or section 951A(c) alone and declined deference under Skidmore due to lack of specific legislative delegation.
Regulatory updates include final regulations from Treasury and IRS: updating qualified domestic trust (QDOT) election procedures; designating certain Charitable Remainder Annuity Trust transactions as listed transactions effective July 9 with reporting requirements; clarifying insurance policy exchanges under section 1035 so such exchanges do not automatically trigger reportable policy sale status but retain consequences from prior sales; streamlining reporting between insurers; maintaining exceptions for certain reorganizations; and confirming compliance with state-law insurable interest requirements.
The Senate Finance Committee will hold a hearing on July 16 regarding nominations for several key Treasury Department positions.
